source_text: Verum quia fidei catholicae, cuius solido nudatus es, quasi amiculum tenue, solum nomen assumis, vis nos credere etiam a te hoc teneri, quod catholici confitentur, id est et liberum arbitrium esse in hominibus et Deum nascentium conditorem. Sed si hoc a te simpliciter fideliterque prolatum est, finem certamini impone silentio; fama ad nos criminantium recurrat, qui id obiecerimus tibi, quod secura negatione deleveris. Hoc solum huic adde sententiae, si qua inventa fuerit secta, si qua disputatio, quae hanc duplicem confessionem, quam catholicam esse professus es, aliqua conetur argumentatione convellere, aut tuam non esse aut a te ulterius non defendi. Si autem iuvat ea, quae dicturus es negasse, locupleti etiam disputatione defendere, explica definitiones liberi arbitrii et fines eius distinctionibus absolutis quasi quibusdam cinge limitibus.
pass_a_gloss: But because stripped of the solid of catholic faith you take up as a thin cloak only the name, you want us to believe that this also is held by you which catholics confess, that is both that there is free choice in humans and that God is the founder of those being born. But if this has been brought forth by you simply and faithfully, place an end on the struggle by silence; let the fame of those accusing run back to us, who have objected to you that which you have deleted by a secure negation. Add only this to this sentence: if any sect has been found, if any disputation, which tries by some argumentation to tear this double confession which you have professed to be catholic, either it is not yours or it is no further defended by you. But if it pleases to defend also by a wealthy disputation those things which you are going to say you have denied, explain the definitions of free choice and gird its boundaries by absolute distinctions as by certain limits.
pass_b_english: But stripped of the substance of catholic faith, you put on its name alone like a thin cloak. You want us to believe that you too hold what catholics confess: that humans have free will and God creates newborn children. If you said this straightforwardly and faithfully, end the dispute by falling silent. Let the reputation of accusers return to us for having charged you with what your confident denial has erased. Add only this to your declaration: if any sect or argument is found trying by some reasoning to overthrow this twofold confession, which you have professed catholic, it is either not yours or no longer defended by you.
If you prefer to defend by substantial argument your denial of the positions in question, explain the definitions of free will and surround its boundaries, as with markers, by precise distinctions.

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Julian claims the catholic faith against Augustine; keep lowercase-c catholic as the universal church, not a later confessional brand.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
